brief: 怒った顔よりも、心配そうな顔にして。家族は「どこにいるんだよ」とセリフを追加。
prompt: Edit the supplied character image, preserving its square composition, four distinct Japanese men, left-to-right order, relative heights, full-body framing, hairstyles, clothing, equipment, and poses. Maintain the same cute chibi cartoon style, thick black outlines, large expressive eyes, and cel-shaded colors. Replace all angry expressions with worried, anxious expressions appropriate to family members and local volunteer firefighters searching for a missing man in Tozawa Village, Yamagata, on the night of May 25, 1988. Raise the inner ends of their eyebrows, soften their eyes with concern, and give them slightly downturned or gently parted mouths. Avoid aggressive scowls, furious narrowed eyes, and confrontational expressions. The second man from the left, wearing a gray windbreaker and carrying a wooden pole, represents a generic family searcher: give him a slightly open mouth as if anxiously calling out for the missing man. His intended dialogue is “どこにいるんだよ” (“Where are you?”), to be added during editing only. Do not render this dialogue or any other text, subtitles, lettering, or speech bubbles in the image. Keep the flashlight, wooden pole, coiled rope, and whistle unchanged. Preserve the transparent background as a standalone character layer; do not replace transparency with black or white. Do not add scenery, people, a bear, or the missing man. These are generic illustrated searchers, not reconstructions of real victims or their relatives. Generate one image.
message: 指示した修正を反映しました。確認してください
